Understanding the Cycle · Free masterclass

What really keeps the binge-purge cycle going, explained by a psychologist

A free, live 60-minute class with Chartered Psychologist Dr Rachel Evans for women who want a clear, kind, psychology-based understanding of the binge-purge cycle and what good support looks like.

Live on Zoom60 minutesReplay includedFree

Dr Rachel Evans PhD

Who this class is for

Gentle, honest education. No judgement.

  • Women who want the binge-purge cycle explained clearly, by someone with the training and the lived experience.
  • People who have read a lot online and want one calm, joined-up explanation.
  • Anyone supporting a loved one who wants to understand what is going on.
  • Anyone curious about what different kinds of support, like 1:1 work and tapping, actually involve.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

Why the cycle is about more than willpower

What psychology research on habits, self-control and behaviour change tells us about why the loop is so persistent.

How shame and the inner critic keep it turning

The quiet thoughts that keep the loop going, and why being harder on yourself rarely helps.

Where beliefs and identity get tangled up

Why it can start to feel like part of who someone is, and how people begin to separate the two.

Calming tools, demonstrated live

A short follow-along tapping (EFT) exercise, so you can see what it involves.

What good support looks like

Self-help, 1:1 work and specialist services: how they differ and how to choose what fits.

Meet Rachel

Hi, I’m Dr Rachel Evans

I’m a Chartered Psychologist with a PhD from the University of Sheffield in the psychology of eating, habits, self-control and behaviour change. I’m also 9+ years recovered from bulimia myself, so I know this from both sides.

I host the Just Eat Normally podcast, and I offer 1:1 support and self-help for women who are ready to break the binge-purge cycle.

Script 1 · “Not willpower”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“The binge-purge cycle is one of the most misunderstood patterns in psychology.”

Body

“I did my PhD on habits, self-control and behaviour change, and here’s what the research keeps showing: this cycle isn’t about willpower. It’s a loop, and loops have parts. Once people can see those parts, it becomes much easier to talk about, and to find the right support.”

CTA

“I’m explaining it in a free live masterclass. Replay included. Tap Sign up to save a seat.”

Shot: talking to camera in natural light, cream background, beige blazer. On-screen text: “not willpower”.

Script 2 · “Both sides”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“I’m a psychologist, and I’ve also lived this myself.”

Body

“So I know the textbook side and the human side. One thing I wish more people understood: shame doesn’t stop the cycle, it feeds it. Understanding is a much kinder place to start.”

CTA

“If you’d like to learn more, I’m running a free educational class. Cameras off, questions anonymous. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: seated, softer and slower. Caption: “Educational content, not medical advice.”

Script 3 · “Why ‘just stop’ doesn’t help”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Why telling someone to ‘just stop’ almost never helps.”

Body

“From the outside it can look simple. From the inside it’s a loop driven by thoughts, feelings and beliefs, not a lack of effort. In my free masterclass I explain how the loop works, and what different kinds of support involve, for anyone who wants to understand it, including people supporting a loved one.”

CTA

“It’s free and live, with a replay. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a simple slide of the loop drawn as a circle.
